candidates.name: HIV-associated lymphoma
support_spans: Medical history included intravenous heroin use 20 years ago by sharing syringes
Recent symptoms included low-grade fever up to 38°C in afternoons, dull left upper abdominal pain, and 3kg weight loss
Spleen palpable 5cm below left costal margin, hard in texture with smooth surface
candidates.why: The patient's history of HIV infection and presentation with systemic symptoms such as fever, abdominal pain, and weight loss, along with splenomegaly, suggest a possible diagnosis of HIV-associated lymphoma.

candidates.name: Tuberculous splenitis
support_spans: Six months prior, he was diagnosed with HIV infection and tuberculous meningitis
Spleen palpable 5cm below left costal margin, hard in texture with smooth surface
candidates.why: The patient's history of tuberculous meningitis and current presentation with splenomegaly suggest a possible diagnosis of tuberculous splenitis.

candidates.name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
support_spans: Splenic biopsy immunohistochemistry: CD20+, Pax5+, BcL-2+, BcL-6+, CD10−, mum-1+, Cmyc+ (40%), CD30+, ALK-, CyclinD1-, CD3−, CD5−, CD2−, CD4−, TIA-1-, GrB-, CD21+, CD34−, PCK-, Ki67+ (80%)
candidates.why: The patient's splenic biopsy immunohistochemistry results suggest a diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

candidates.name: Castleman disease
support_spans: Splenomegaly with multiple occupying lesions
Large spleen with uneven density, S4 liver nodules, multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with splenomegaly, multiple occupying lesions, and hypermetabolic lymph nodes suggests a possible diagnosis of Castleman disease.

candidates.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
support_spans: Splenic biopsy immunohistochemistry: CD20+, Pax5+, BcL-2+, BcL-6+, CD10−, mum-1+, Cmyc+ (40%), CD30+, ALK-, CyclinD1-, CD3−, CD5−, CD2−, CD4−, TIA-1-, GrB-, CD21+, CD34−, PCK-, Ki67+ (80%)
candidates.why: The patient's splenic biopsy immunohistochemistry results, including CD30 positivity, suggest a possible diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma.

candidates.name: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
support_spans: Multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes
Multiple foci of metabolic hyperplasia in right iliac bone, right acetabulum, left pubic bone and bilateral femur
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes and foci of metabolic hyperplasia in various bones suggests a possible diagnosis of lymphomatoid granulomatosis.
